name: The Artillery Yard
summary: A great hooped bombard lashed into its sledge, a pyramid of stone gunstones, powder kegs, and the powder cart with its spare wheel and rammer rack.
description: Where the old castle stabled horses, the new one stables guns. The bombard in the north-west corner is wrought-iron staves hooped like a barrel, with a narrower powder chamber behind the bore, and it lies roped into a timber sledge because nothing on wheels could carry it. Its ammunition is stone, cut round by masons and stacked in a pyramid across the yard; each ball is the weight of a man. Powder lives in kegs in the far corner, as far from anything that burns as the gunners can manage, and the two-wheeled cart that brings it stands ready with a spare wheel against the wall and the rammer and sponge racked above. One spark in the south-east corner and the yard is a crater.
build: Shell: the kit's OuterBailey shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m dressed-sandstone walls 3.60 m clear, a 0.45 m brick trim course, an archway 2.60 × 2.59 m centred on every wall.
Sledge (NW): oak 3.00 × 0.90 × 0.35 m at (−3.60, 4.20), long axis east–west; three oak cleats 0.12 × 0.90 × 0.50 m across it at x −4.74 / −3.54 / −2.34.

Bombard: an iron powder chamber r 0.25 m, 1.00 m long (x −5.10 … −4.10), and the bore r 0.36 m, 1.90 m long (x −4.10 … −2.20), axis at 0.95 m above ground, muzzle east; seven iron hoops r 0.38 m along the bore; a soot disc in the muzzle; two rope lashings round barrel and sledge.
Gunstones (NE): stone balls r 0.22 m in a 3-2-1 square pyramid centred (3.60, 4.20), each layer settled 0.02 m into the one below; two loose balls at (2.30, 3.20) and (2.75, 3.20).

Powder kegs (SE): five oak kegs r 0.25 m, 0.50 m tall, two iron hoops each, at (3.20, −4.80), (3.75, −4.80), (4.30, −4.80), (3.45, −4.25), (4.00, −4.25); a sixth lying east–west across three of them at (3.75, −4.52), 0.80–1.30 m above ground.

Powder cart (SW): an oak bed 1.60 × 0.90 × 0.10 m, top 0.85 m above the floor, at (−3.20, −3.80) on two supports and an iron axle; two spoked wheels r 0.45 m; two short shafts 0.70 m pointing east, ending at x −1.85.
Spare wheel: a spoked oak wheel r 0.45 m standing against the west wall at y −3.40.
Rammer rack: two iron brackets on the south wall at x −4.80 and −2.60; an oak rammer and a linen-headed sponge, each on a 3.00 m pole, at 1.55 and 1.90 m above ground.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.59 m (OuterBailey), all open
Keg tops: two loot anchors at 0.80 m
Powder cart bed: a loot anchor at 1.15 m

materials.name: Wrought iron
materials.notes: Bombard barrel and chamber; hoops in line.

gameplay: The powder kegs are the Late bailey's bomb: fire in the SE corner detonates them.
The bombard is scenery too heavy to move, and the best cover in the yard.
Three loot anchors: two kegs and the cart.
